India competed at the 2026 Asian Games in Nagoya, Aichi Prefecture, Japan from 19 September to 4 October 2026.[1] This was the country's 20th consecutive appearance in the competition, having made its debut at the inaugural 1951 Asian Games. The Indian contingent consisted of 495 athletes competing in 36 sports. Sports shooter Manu Bhaker and kabaddi player Pawan Sehrawat were the nation's flag-bearers during the opening ceremony. Shooter Neeru Dhanda was the flag-bearer for the closing ceremony. India finished fourth in the medal table with 85 medals including 21 gold, 27 silver, and 37 bronze medals. It was India's second highest medal tally at the Asian Games after the 2022 edition.

Background

[edit]

The Indian Olympic Association (IOA) was established in 1927 and recognised by the International Olympic Committee in the same year.[2] India was one of the founding members of the Asian Games Federation (AGF), established on 13 February 1949.[3][4] On 26 November 1981, the Olympic Council of Asia (OCA) replaced the AGF,[4] and India became a member of the OCA.[5]

India hosted the first Asian Games in 1951 at New Delhi.[3] The 2026 Asian Games were held in Nagoya and other parts of Aichi Prefecture in Japan from 19 September to 4 October.[6] The 2026 edition marked India's 20th consecutive appearance at the Asian Games. India's best performance came in the 2023 Asian Games at Hangzhou where the country finished fourth in the medal table with 106 medals including 28 gold, 38 silver, 40 bronze medals.[7]

On 22 August 2026, the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports announced a 492-member Indian contingent for the Games.[1] On 2 September 2026, the ministry released a revised list of 503 athletes and 265 support staff for the Games.[8] The final traveling contingent consisted of 495 athletes.[9][10] Sahdev Yadav, the treasurer of the IOA, was the Chef de Mission with Sharath Kamal chosen as his deputy.[11] On 18 September 2026, Manu Bhaker and Tajinderpal Singh Toor were announced as the nation's flag-bearers during the opening ceremony.[12] However, Toor withdrew from the opening ceremony after the arrival of his kit was delayed and was replaced by Pawan Sehrawat as the flag bearer.[13] Shooter Neeru Dhanda was the flag-bearer for the closing ceremony.[14]

Broadcasting

[edit]

Sony Pictures Networks acquired the broadcast rights for the country, with Sony Sports Network as the television broadcaster and SonyLIV as the digital broadcaster.[15]

Medal summary

[edit]
Main article: 2026 Asian Games medal table

India finished fourth in the medal table with 85 medals including 21 gold, 27 silver, and 37 bronze medals. It was their 2nd best finish ever after the 2022 edition.[7][16]

Archery

[edit]
Main article: Archery at the 2026 Asian Games

The Archery Association of India held the selection trials for the Asian Games at the Sports Authority of India (SAI) facility in Sonipat in May 2026.[17] A total of 12 athletes were selected across the recurve and compound events.[18]

Athletics

[edit]
Further information: Athletics at the 2026 Asian Games

India initially announced a 79-member squad to compete in the athletic events.[8] Runner Abhishek Pal failed a dope test,[19] hurdler Tejas Shirse pulled out due to an injury,[20] and Annu Rani, Nithya Gandhe, and Shahnavaz Khan were dropped from the squad.[21][22] Javelin thrower Yashvir Singh replaced the injured Neeraj Chopra,[23] while long jumper David Solomon replaced Khan.[24] The final squad consisted of 75 athletes competing in 41 events.[25] On 26 September 2026, Jyothi Yarraji did not compete in the women's 100 m hurdles heats, and Praveen Chithravel pulled out after his first jump in the men's triple jump due to an injury.[26][27]

Cricket

[edit]
Main article: Cricket at the 2026 Asian Games

Both the men's and women's cricket teams qualified for the Games as full members of the International Cricket Council. The Board of Control for Cricket in India announced the 15-member men's squad on 6 June 2026, which was captained by Shreyas Iyer and coached by VVS Laxman.[32][33] The women's squad, led by Harmanpreet Kaur, was announced on 30 June.[34] Subsequently, Harshit Rana and Varun Chakravarthy were replaced by Yash Thakur and Vipraj Nigam respectively due to injuries and Nitish Kumar Reddy was withdrawn from the men's squad.[35][36] In the women's squad, Jemimah Rodrigues was ruled out due to an injury and replaced by Pratika Rawal.[37] The men's team received a bye in the preliminary stage and directly qualified for the knockout stage.[38]

Equestrian

[edit]
Main article: Equestrian at the 2026 Asian Games

The Equestrian Federation of India selected a 12-member squad for the three disciplines at the Games in June 2026.[42] The show jumping team was omitted from the final list, which reduced the squad strength to eight.[1] Aahan Kumar, who was supposed to compete in the eventing competitions, was unable to participate after his horse, Bolivar Gio Granno, tested positive for Piroplasmosis a few weeks before the Games.[43]

Judo

[edit]
Main article: Judo at the 2026 Asian Games

The judo selection trials for the Games were held in February 2026 at the K. D. Jadhav Indoor Hall in Delhi,[51] with 12 athletes qualifying. However, the sports ministry later excluded several athletes (nine) from the initial list including 2026 Commonwealth Games medalists Harsh Singh and Unnati Sharma, and approved a final list of three judokas for the Games.[52]
